nodes.label: Respect language (keigo) vs. neutral language — basic distinction
nodes.rationale: A speaker can direct respect toward the 2nd person (addressee), a 3rd person discussed, or both.
nodes.norm_label: respect language (keigo) vs. neutral language — basic distinction

nodes.label: Polite words vs. respectful words — terminological distinction
nodes.rationale: Polite words (watakushi, ikaga, dochira) raise general tone for the addressee's impression; respectful words (kata, anata, donata) target a specific person.
nodes.norm_label: polite words vs. respectful words — terminological distinction

nodes.label: The "situation diagram" framework (circled 1/2/3 person, R/N arrows, outsider square)
nodes.rationale: Core analytical device of the whole book: respect flows upward by relative seniority within one's circle; defaults to respectful toward outsiders; in-circle 3rd persons are not shown respect when discussed with an outsider.
nodes.norm_label: the "situation diagram" framework (circled 1/2/3 person, r/n arrows, outsider square)

nodes.label: Honorific vs. depreciatory verbs — the "see-saw principle"
nodes.rationale: An honorific verb raises its own subject's status; if the respected person is not the subject, status is instead lowered on the other side of the see-saw (depreciatory verbs).
nodes.norm_label: honorific vs. depreciatory verbs — the "see-saw principle"

nodes.label: -masu endings show respect to the addressee independently of honorific-verb choice
nodes.rationale: Honorific verbs target the grammatical subject; masu targets the 2nd person — these are independent axes that can combine or diverge.
nodes.norm_label: -masu endings show respect to the addressee independently of honorific-verb choice

nodes.label: The "involvement" test licensing a depreciatory verb/prefix
nodes.rationale: A depreciatory form is only usable when the respected person is genuinely involved in the verb's action (as giver/recipient), not merely an onlooker.
nodes.norm_label: the "involvement" test licensing a depreciatory verb/prefix

nodes.label: Chōdai and systematic final-verb ellipsis in casual permissive requests
nodes.rationale: A fully explicit polite-permissive sentence sheds its outer layers down to a bare fragment while retaining pragmatic politeness force.
nodes.norm_label: chodai and systematic final-verb ellipsis in casual permissive requests

nodes.label: The permissive (-te morau/itadaku) construction as Japan's preferred indirect-request idiom
nodes.rationale: Japanese systematically prefers an indirect, permission-framed request form where English tolerates a direct volitional one.
nodes.norm_label: the permissive (-te morau/itadaku) construction as japan's preferred indirect-request idiom

nodes.label: Yaru vs. ageru signal relative status of the permissive construction's indirect beneficiary
nodes.rationale: Japan's give/receive verb system encodes relative social status as a structural, obligatory grammatical choice rather than an optional stylistic one.
nodes.norm_label: yaru vs. ageru signal relative status of the permissive construction's indirect beneficiary

nodes.label: Deferential verbs defined and distinguished from depreciatory verbs
nodes.rationale: A deferential verb is a depreciatory-type verb so inherently respectful it is used only toward the 2nd person, virtually never the 3rd.
nodes.norm_label: deferential verbs defined and distinguished from depreciatory verbs

nodes.label: Resolving a "social dilemma": combining deferential/depreciatory verbs with the honorific passive
nodes.rationale: Stacking two normally separate politeness devices (depreciation + honorific passive) onto one verb to satisfy two simultaneous, otherwise-conflicting politeness obligations.
nodes.norm_label: resolving a "social dilemma": combining deferential/depreciatory verbs with the honorific passive

nodes.label: Omi- — a compound honorific prefix surviving only in fossilized honorific nouns (omi-ashi, omi-kuji, omi-otsuke)
nodes.rationale: A once-productive honorific morphological pattern surviving only in lexicalized fossils.
nodes.norm_label: omi- — a compound honorific prefix surviving only in fossilized honorific nouns (omi-ashi, omi-kuji, omi-otsuke)

nodes.label: Duplicate-resolution methodology for the Busy People I/II PDF set
nodes.rationale: Four related PDFs (Kana Textbook, Romanized Textbook, two Kana Workbook editions) plus a separate Book II were compared side-by-side before extraction; script-variant and edition duplicates were identified and skipped (older 77pp workbook, Romanized Textbook) so extraction effort was not wasted on redundant content, while the genuinely separate Book II was kept as a distinct source.
nodes.norm_label: duplicate-resolution methodology for the busy people i/ii pdf set

nodes.label: Font-cipher-corrupted text layer forcing full vision-read extraction
nodes.rationale: pdftotext produced scrambled Latin symbol soup with no recoverable 1:1 substitution (confirmed not a simple keyboard/offset cipher), so the entire course was vision-read from rendered 150dpi page images instead of trusting any OCR/text layer, to avoid silently encoding garbage as vocabulary.
nodes.norm_label: font-cipher-corrupted text layer forcing full vision-read extraction

nodes.label: Page-spread scan gotcha: one PDF page = two printed pages
nodes.rationale: Each PDF page image is a scanned two-printed-page spread (PDF page n≥4 shows printed pages 2n−4 left and 2n−3 right); this offset was verified empirically against printed page numbers rather than assumed, to avoid mis-citing page numbers for every extracted item.
nodes.norm_label: page-spread scan gotcha: one pdf page = two printed pages

nodes.label: JBridge to Intermediate Japanese pagination gotcha (two facing pages per PDF page)
nodes.rationale: The main PDF's near-2:1 landscape page size scans two facing printed pages per PDF page (e.g. PDF page 9 = printed pages 2 and 3 as one wide image); caught by direct inspection rather than assumed from pdfinfo alone, flagged explicitly as 'the same class of issue the extraction spec already flags for other vision-only sources' so page citations would not be silently doubled or mis-numbered.
nodes.norm_label: jbridge to intermediate japanese pagination gotcha (two facing pages per pdf page)
